Accessibility Testing.C: Inspect page headings, task titles, descriptions, table headings, navigation links, buttons and smaller text on My Tasks.
Accessibility Testing.D: Text should be readable and presented clearly without difficulty.
Accessibility Testing.E: All inspected text elements were generally readable, with font sizes and appearances that allowed the information to be understood without difficulty.
Accessibility Testing.H: Readable text improves accessibility and helps users understand the information presented.

Accessibility Testing.C: Inspect text and background colours, buttons and task status indicators on My Tasks.
Accessibility Testing.D: Text and status indicators should be sufficiently distinguishable to support readability and accessibility.
Accessibility Testing.E: The Done and Open statuses have similar background colours, making them difficult to distinguish by colour alone. However, the strikethrough applied to completed task titles provides an additional visual indicator.
Accessibility Testing.H: Improve the visual distinction between Open and Done statuses using more distinguishable colours while retaining the strikethrough indicator.

Accessibility Testing.C: Navigate through interactive elements using Tab and Shift + Tab without using a mouse. Observe keyboard focus indicators.
Accessibility Testing.D: Users should be able to navigate interactive elements using the keyboard, with a visible focus indicator.
Accessibility Testing.E: The interactive elements could be navigated using Tab and Shift + Tab, and the currently focused element was visibly highlighted.
Accessibility Testing.H: Keyboard navigation and visible focus indicators support users who rely on keyboard interaction.

Accessibility Testing.C: Inspect the Title, Description, Category and Due Date fields on the New Task page.
Accessibility Testing.D: Each form field should have a clear, visible label identifying its purpose.
Accessibility Testing.E: All inspected form fields had clear and visible labels that identified the information users needed to enter.
Accessibility Testing.H: Clear form labels help users identify the purpose of each input field.

Accessibility Testing.B: Evaluate clarity of input validation messages
Accessibility Testing.C: Submit the New Task form without entering any details and observe the validation message.
Accessibility Testing.D: Validation messages should clearly explain the input requirements and guide users on how to correct invalid submissions.
Accessibility Testing.E: The browser displayed “Please fill out this field” and prevented submission. However, the message only highlighted the Title field and did not provide broader guidance that a task title is required before submission.
Accessibility Testing.H: Provide clearer and more informative validation feedback, such as “Please enter a task title before creating the task.”

Accessibility Testing.C: Inspect headings, page sections and grouping of information on My Tasks and Dashboard.
Accessibility Testing.D: Headings and page sections should be organised logically to help users understand the interface structure.
Accessibility Testing.E: The headings and page sections were logically organised, making the information easy to follow and understand.
Accessibility Testing.H: A clear interface structure helps users locate information and understand the organisation of the application.

Accessibility Testing.C: Inspect buttons and links on My Tasks and New Task pages, including their labels and purposes.
Accessibility Testing.D: Buttons and links should be identifiable and have understandable labels describing their purposes.
Accessibility Testing.E: The buttons and links were clearly identifiable, with text that explained their purposes.
Accessibility Testing.H: Clearly labelled interactive elements help users understand and interact with the application.

Summary.A: 1. Open and Done task statuses have similar background colours; the strikethrough provides an additional visual indicator.
2. The empty-title validation message prevents submission but could provide more informative guidance.

This is a basic accessibility review using selected WCAG-related concepts. It is not a full WCAG conformance audit or certification.

Compatibility Testing.C: Open Microsoft Edge → Navigate to http://127.0.0.1:5000/ → Log in → Open My Tasks.
Compatibility Testing.D: Application interface should display correctly without visual or layout issues.

Compatibility Testing.B: Verify application functionality in Microsoft Edge
Compatibility Testing.C: Open My Tasks in Edge → Click New Task → Enter valid task details (Edge Compatibility Test; Personal; leave Due Date blank) → Click Create Task.
Compatibility Testing.D: The task should be created successfully and displayed in the task list.

Compatibility Testing.C: Maximise Microsoft Edge → Set browser zoom to 100% → Open My Tasks → Inspect interface elements.
Compatibility Testing.D: Application elements should display properly without overlapping, clipping or horizontal scrolling.

Compatibility Testing.B: Verify layout at smaller screen resolution
Compatibility Testing.C: Restore browser window → Resize to a narrower width → Keep zoom at 100% → Open My Tasks.
Compatibility Testing.D: Application elements should remain accessible and adjust to the smaller browser window without major overlapping or clipping.
Compatibility Testing.E: Task information and action links remained visible. Text wrapped onto multiple lines, and a vertical scrollbar appeared.
Compatibility Testing.H: The layout remained usable at a smaller window width, although some elements became cramped and text wrapping affected readability.

Compatibility Testing.B: Verify form and button alignment at smaller window size
Compatibility Testing.C: Resize browser window → Open New Task → Inspect form fields and buttons.
Compatibility Testing.D: Form fields and buttons should remain visible, aligned and accessible without overlapping or horizontal clipping.
Compatibility Testing.E: All form fields and buttons remained visible and properly aligned. No overlapping or horizontal scrolling was observed.
Compatibility Testing.H: The form maintained its alignment and usability at the tested smaller browser window size. A vertical scrollbar was available.

Summary.B: Two browsers (Google Chrome and Microsoft Edge) and desktop/smaller browser-window configurations were tested. Physical mobile devices and multiple native screen resolutions were not tested.
